'''Irene R. Schloss''' is an [[Antarctic]] researcher, best known for her work on plankton biology. She is a researcher at the [[Instituto Antártico Argentino|Argentine Antarctic Institute]] and was a  correspondent researcher of the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|National Scientific and Technical Research Council of Argentina]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ismer.ca/Schloss-Irene-R?lang=fr|title=Schloss, Irene R. - Institut des sciences de la mer de Rimouski|website=www.ismer.ca|access-date=2016-06-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819102535/http://www.ismer.ca/Schloss-Irene-R?lang=fr|archive-date=2016-08-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> until July 2017. She became an independent researcher since August 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Irene_Schloss2|title=Irene SCHLOSS {{!}} PhD {{!}} Instituto Antártico Argentino {{!}} Instituto Antártico Argentino, Buenos Aires {{!}} IAA|website=ResearchGate|language=en|access-date=2020-03-13}}</ref> and an associate professor at the [[University of Quebec]].

==Early life and education==
Schloss was born in [[Buenos Aires]], Argentina, where she first completed her “[[Licentiate (degree)|Licenciatura]]” (equivalent to a MSc) in Biology at the [[University of Buenos Aires]]. In 1989 she undertook a fellowship for 6 months ([[International Association for the Exchange of Students for Technical Experience|IAESTE]] and DAAD) at the [[Alfred Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research|Alfred-Wegener Institute]] in [[Bremerhaven]], Germany, participating in the international European “Polarstern” Study (EPOS).<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://epic.awi.de/26242/|title=The expedition Antarktis VII/3 (EPOS LEG 2) of RV "Polarstern" in 1988/89|date=1989|website=epic.awi.de|publisher=Alfred Wegener Institute|doi=10.2312/BzP_0065_1989 |access-date= |last1=Hempel |first1=Irmtraut |last2=Schalk |first2=Peter H. |last3=Smetacek |first3=Victor |page=199 }}</ref> She then began her PhD in 1992 as a National Council of the Research (CONICET) fellow in biological oceanography. Throughout her PhD she studied phytoplankton dynamics in coastal Antarctica. She received her PhD degree from the [[University of Buenos Aires]] in 1997.<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://digital.bl.fcen.uba.ar/Download/Tesis/Tesis_2952_Schloss.pdf|title=Escalas temporo-espaciales de variabilidad del fitoplancton costero Antártico|last=Schloss|first=Irene|date=1997|website=|publisher=Universidad de Buenos Aires|trans-title=Temporo-spatial scales of variability in Antarctic coastal phytoplankton|type=Thesis|access-date=}}</ref> Between 2005 and 2007, she was a post-doctoral fellow at ISMER, where she studied the dynamics of phytoplankton and physical – biological coupling in the [[Beaufort Sea]] ([[Northern Canada|Canadian Arctic]]).<ref name=":1" />

==Career and impact==
Schloss is a researcher at the Argentinian Antarctic Institute (IAA) and is a Correspondent Researcher of the National Council of the Research (CONICET) of Argentina.<ref name=":0" /> She has been an associate professor at [[Université du Québec à Rimouski|UQAR]] since 2009, and was a research assistant there since 2008.<ref name=":1" /> Her research focuses on the impact of UVB radiation on plankton communities at a range of latitudes, the role of phytoplankton on CO<sub>2</sub> fluxes between the ocean and the atmosphere and the effects of global change on coastal plankton.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ismer.ca/Schloss-Irene-R?lang=fr|title=Schloss, Irene R.|website=www.ismer.ca|publisher=Institut des sciences de la mer de Rimouski|access-date=2016-06-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819102535/http://www.ismer.ca/Schloss-Irene-R?lang=fr|archive-date=2016-08-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has research expertise in the dynamics of high latitude marine plankton and variations of plankton communities in space and time. Schloss has participated in nine expeditions to Antarctica (ship-based and on Argentinean stations), spending around 17 months in the sixth continent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scar.org/srp/ant-era#Carlini16|title=Studying the effect of warming oceans and glacier melting on Antarctic plankton.|last=|first=|website=www.scar.org|publisher=Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research|access-date=2016-06-14}}</ref>

Her greatest impact has been in research on the interactions the adaptation and effects of plankton to ocean [[climate change]]. Her work has modelled physical-biological interactions during bloom dynamics in coastal Antarctica, in particular the equilibrium between warming, glacier melt water and wind-induced physical turbulence in coastal waters. Her work on the role of plankton groups on CO<sub>2</sub> dynamics indicated that [[diatoms]] are key contributors to atmospheric CO<sub>2</sub> uptake in surface waters, providing a direct link between biodiversity and climate-relevant processes. Additionally, her work demonstrated links between large-scale atmospheric phenomena (e.g. [[Southern Annular Mode]] and [[El Niño Southern Oscillation]]) and local phytoplankton dynamics.

Schloss plays a central role in the development of international collaborations in Antarctic research.<ref name=":1" /> She has been successful in working in polar science in different countries, such as Argentina, Canada, and Germany through the promotion and participation in numerous international research projects and initiatives, cooperating with researchers from USA, Spain, Belgium, Brazil, Poland, and the UK.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imconet.eu/about-the-project/work-packages/wp-2.html|title=Climate change effects on coastal polar environments and on planktonic communities|website=imconet.eu|publisher=Interdisciplinary Modelling of Climate Change in Coastal Western Antarctica Network|access-date=2016-06-14}}</ref> She further participates in the development of the Antarctic Environmental Portal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.environments.aq/information-summaries/vulnerability-of-southern-ocean-biota-to-climate-change/|title=Vulnerability of Southern Ocean biota to climate change|website=www.environments.aq|publisher=Antarctic Environments Portal|access-date=2016-06-14|archive-date=2019-10-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191023210602/https://www.environments.aq/information-summaries/vulnerability-of-southern-ocean-biota-to-climate-change/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  She is particularly involved in the promotion of Antarctic science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scar.org/antera/antera-about|title=Antarctic Thresholds - Ecosystem Resilience and Adaptation|last=|first=|website=www.scar.org|publisher=Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research|access-date=2016-06-14|archive-date=2017-11-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117083105/https://www.scar.org/antera/antera-about/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She participated at the SCAR Horizon SCAN in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scar.org/horizonscan/retreat/attendees|title=Horizon Scan Retreat|last=|first=|date=2014|website=www.scar.org|publisher=Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research|access-date=2016-06-14|archive-date=2016-04-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405104455/http://www.scar.org/horizonscan/retreat/attendees|url-status=dead}}</ref>
